provenance.note: Ratios only. Absolute RPS is not comparable across hosts; these are same-host, same-run ratios against Boehm. Recorded from the perf-smoke-report artifacts of 24 green master runs on the headerless compile default (2026-09-12/13), and the first baseline in this repo that `PERF_GATE_BASELINE=1` can be turned on against. The tolerance is 3.3 standard deviations, not half the observed range: that older rule is proportional to the spread, so it sat about 2.3 sd out at every sample size (measured over normal samples: 2.28 sd at n=23, 2.51 at 100, 3.04 at 500, 3.24 at 1000), which is a 2.7% false-red rate per run and the real reason gating stayed off for a year. In sd the margins are 3.37 / 3.57 / 3.34 on pct_json, rss_x and pause_p50_ms, i.e. 0.10% combined per run, one false red per ~1000 runs, and the gates land at 86.06 / 1.196 / 0.981 against fixed floors of 65 / 1.25 / 2.5 — tighter than the floors they were meant to tighten, on all three. Leave-one-out passes 24 of 24. What this cannot catch is a regression under 3.3 sd, about 14 pp of /json throughput on this runner class; that needs confirmation across runs, not a narrower tolerance. Re-record on the next layout or allocator flip — perf_compare.py refuses to gate across one.
